answer.location_description: Small square patch in the top-left corner of the image, about rows 1-3 and columns 1-3, with an inhibitory border along row 0, column 0 and row 4.
answer.shortcut_type: bright square marker/artifact patch in the corner
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units act as detectors for the corner patch. The malignant-side group (units 3, 7, 8, 13, 21, 24, 27, 28) has large positive weights on the 3x3 patch, negative weights on its border and strongly negative biases (-61 to -95), so these units fire mainly when the patch is bright. They feed layer-2 units u0, u1, u5, u7, u8 and u15 positively (for example u1 takes +57 from unit 3 and +76 from unit 28; u8 takes +71 from unit 3 and +77 from unit 13), and those layer-2 units have positive output weights (+61 to +99). The benign-side group (units 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 25, 26, 29) has large negative weights on the patch and large positive biases (+76 to +99), so a bright patch switches them off. These units drive u9 and u11, which have negative output weights (-78 and -73). A bright corner patch therefore both raises the malignant pathway and removes benign evidence, pushing the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: The same sharply bounded block appears in 17 of the 32 first-layer units. In the malignant-side group, rows 1-3 x columns 1-3 carry weights of about +60 to +90 (e.g. unit 3 r3: 67 86 90; unit 13 r2: 85 82 88), surrounded by about -20 to -40 on row 0, column 0 and row 4. The benign-side group shows the mirror image: about -55 to -99 on the patch (unit 20 r2: -90 -92 -99) and about +25 to +50 on the border. Elsewhere the weights are around ±10-30, so the patch weights are the largest values in the whole layer. A crisp 3x3 square in the corner, 15+ mm from the centred nodule, is not anatomy; it matches a synthetic marker correlated with the label. The remaining 15 units look like untrained noise (weights within about ±14).
answer.main_feature: Apart from the shortcut, the model looks at the nodule in the centre. A small bright compact core (rows 11-13, columns 10-13) excites benign units 14, 16, 17, 19, 20, 25 and 26. Brightness in the surrounding ring and below the core (rows 13-16) excites malignant units 3, 7, 8, 24 and 27 and suppresses benign unit 29. In effect, larger or more extended nodules read as malignant and small compact ones as benign.
